claims.claim: Le Guin, quoting her own Steering the Craft, says writers who want to take responsibility are wary of the passive voice.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin quoting Steering the Craft pp. 56-57, in 'Navigating the Ocean of Story - Session 1, Part 3' (2015)
claims.quote: Writers who want to take responsibility are wary of it.
claims.page: answer to Christy; she cites Steering the Craft pp. 56-57

claims.claim: Le Guin says the passive voice ought to be used freely where it belongs and calls it one of the lovely versatilities of the verb.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin quoting Steering the Craft pp. 56-57, in 'Navigating the Ocean of Story - Session 1, Part 3' (2015)
claims.quote: It is one of the lovely versatilities of the verb.
claims.page: answer to Christy; she cites Steering the Craft pp. 56-57

claims.claim: Le Guin offers the walking story, in which you cover ground while seeing everything around you, as an alternative to the fast-paced suspenseful one.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'What Makes a Story' (c. 2007), ursulakleguin.com
claims.quote: steady, and you fall into the flow of the gait

claims.claim: Le Guin defines a writer as a person who cares what words mean.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, 'A Few Words to a Young Writer' (undated), ursulakleguin.com
claims.quote: A writer is a person who cares what words mean

claims.claim: Le Guin says the grammar words subject, predicate, object, adjective, adverb and the tenses are the names of the writer's tools.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, introduction to the 2015 revision of Steering the Craft, quoted on ursulakleguin.com
claims.quote: these are the names of the writer’s tools
